subject: feat(attn): add native KVarN cache and compact K4V2 attention

requirement.feature: Native Xe2 KVarN K4V4/K4V2 packed-record writing, DPAS layout, Hadamard/scatter, compact-cache decode, bounded materialization and output reduction; independent record/reference/replay tests
requirement.active_workload: B70/Xe2, dense Qwen3.8-27B W4A16 target with compact K4V2 D256/G128 cache, V2/DFlash2 and RAM prefixes. Existing supported K4V4, padded records and numerical reference paths remain within retained feature scope.
requirement.net_effect: Assigned commit is the final old kernel tip. No later local repair or revert changes its contribution. Its commit already folds the released format/reader refinements and removes the unused coordinate-loader experiment.
requirement.removal_consequence: The paired vLLM KVarN backend loses required _vllm_fa2_C operators and compact-record support. Ordinary BF16/FP8 attention and the upstream CPU cache tier do not substitute for this record format or its memory reduction.

upstream_coverage.evidence: Selected kernel target is unchanged, so it adds no implementation. git grep over frozen vLLM v0.33 and kernel v0.1.17 finds no KVarN/K4V2 implementation. Upstream Sinkhorn mentions are MHC gating, not quantized KV-record balancing. Neither target supplies KVarNLayout, compact 26880-byte K4V2 records, the DPAS bit packing, FP16 resident-tail ownership, or matching native writer/decode/materialize operators.
upstream_coverage.decision: KEEP. No semantic upstream replacement was demonstrated.

upstream_coverage.evidence: New block_2d_align.hpp and edits in chunk_prefill_mainloop.hpp/chunk_prefill_epilogue.hpp align ordinary per-head Q/K/V/O 2D surfaces for nonstandard head widths such as MoonViT H72. Our resident-tail optimization is inside KVarNDecodeFwdMainloop and conditionally loads FP16 tail slots using its own storage contract, with a scalar fallback for unaligned base views. The new helper neither decodes KVarN records nor reaches the custom resident-tail reader automatically.
upstream_coverage.decision: Not superseding. If a newer kernel base is selected later, reconcile overlapping generic epilogue edits and preserve upstream alignment rather than replaying old epilogue bodies wholesale; reuse of the helper would need explicit source and numerical review. No adaptation is needed on the selected unchanged base.

upstream_coverage.evidence: The newer Python FlashAttention wrapper handles ragged speculative queries against ordinary paged K/V. KVarN callers use separate compact-cache native decode/materialization operators, and their unpaged materialized fallback is not this paged redirect. This does not replace the quantized record ABI, resident tails or custom output reduction.
upstream_coverage.decision: No feature deletion or new current-profile speed claim. v0.33 GDN/KVarN adaptive-verification compatibility remains a separate issue documented by the host performance audit.

upstream_coverage.area: Optional local split reduction and resident loads
upstream_coverage.evidence: These are local optimizations rather than essential record-format semantics. The selected upstream base is unchanged and newer upstream does not provide their custom-reader/reducer equivalents. Existing docs/fork-delta.md records about 3% in one historical short reducer cell, an unresolved 3.67% K4V4 regression, stronger historical K4V2 resident-load evidence and a short K4V4 anomaly. No fresh controlled with/without result was obtained in this audit.
upstream_coverage.decision: Retain the existing qualified implementation while preserving fallback/reference paths. Do not report a newly established speedup. Their future removal can be independent of the KVarN format but needs a controlled comparison covering both K4V2 and K4V4, not absence of a merge conflict or smaller commit count.

minimum_residual: Keep this single coherent native feature commit unchanged at the selected kernel base; no temporary follow-up commits or base bump are required.
Keep the XE2-gated native schemas, CMake source registration and MIXED_GRF_SIZE behavior used by this attention library.
Keep both value-bit-width contracts, compact/padded layout reference tests, alignment fallbacks and stream-lifetime distinctions.
Keep the currently qualified optional optimizations with their limited evidence explicitly recorded; no new performance claim is made.

dependencies.contract: KVarN backend's writer, scatter, decode and materialization call sites must match the retained native schemas. vllm/v1/attention/backends/kvarn_attn.py and ops/triton_kvarn_decode.py supply value_bits, dpas_layout, split count, block-to-tail slots and caller-owned scratch. Native decode validates D256/G128/Hq24/Hkv4 geometry, variant18, exact multi-split scratch layout and nonaliasing. The exp_sums tensor stores split LSE; legacy max_logits remains validated/stream-tracked for ABI compatibility.

The split attention library must include all KVarN sources and the FA2 glue must register them under VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XE2. Brutus retains BMG AOT selection. Package identity/build checks remain necessary even when the kernel source tip is unchanged.

performed: Read assigned patch and final old-tip implementation; stable patch ID recorded above.
Inspected selected/newer upstream symbols and affected attention diffs, including ordinary surface alignment and adaptive verification alternatives.

33 CPU tests passed in2.47s: test_kvarn_layout.py, test_kvarn_compact_record.py, test_kvarn_dpas_layout.py, test_kvarn_qkv_scatter_static.py and test_kvarn_reader_variants_static.py. Ran through the uv-created candidate .venv with --noconftest, no pytest cache and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1; both torch.xpu._lazy_init and torch.cuda._lazy_init were replaced by rejecting guards. No accelerator initialized.
validation.cpu_test_scope: Independent packed-record byte/coordinate/scale behavior plus source-level lifetime/reader address checks. These do not establish native numerical execution or performance.
required_after_operator_handoff: Run installed native K4V2/K4V4 record writer/dequant/scatter/materialization/decode reference and replay cases, including compact strides, ragged lengths, split16/fused output, aligned and offset tail buffers, shortened verification and boundary requests.
Test the rebased vLLM candidate's real target/draft ownership, RAM replay, reset and context-ceiling behavior against the retained native ABI.
Use matched old/new host serving measurements for throughput, TTFT, RAM-prefix restore and peak memory; source-equivalent kernels do not qualify changed vLLM scheduling/planning.
If changing optional reducers or resident loads, separately compare with/without on K4V2 and K4V4. Existing whole-profile qualification is not isolated optimization evidence.
